description: Directory resolution (SPEC §8.2.5-§8.2.6, 0.4.0) over checked facts: each record's signing key, each address's binding read (the keys it binds, or no answer), each claim's anchor (vc23) and coin read. The reader walks live listings in (anchor, claim_id) order; the first time it meets an address it reads which keys are bound, and the address's state is its freshest record signed by a bound key; a listing whose address state carries its claim, not ended by a bound tombstone, has its coin read, and the first that passes holds. A read without an answer before the holder is E_DIR_UNRESOLVED. A record found only on public relays is an audit claim with bounds of its own, and its reads count against those alone; the first audit claim the walk cannot finish ends the audit. `reads` lists the reads made, in order.

cases.name: later funded claimant ignored
cases.why: The first anchored claim that passes holds; the later one is never read.

cases.name: unanchored claims cost no read
cases.why: A pending proof, or an anchor with 5 confirmations, is dropped before any read (§8.2.5 (1)).

cases.name: a spend releases the handle once the re-point window has passed
cases.why: §8.2.2 (3): the coin moved and dir_repoint_blocks + 6 = 1014 confirmations passed with no re-point (§8.2.9), so the next claim holds.

cases.name: a spend inside the re-point window does not
cases.why: §8.2.2 (3): at 1013 confirmations the holder can still re-point (§8.2.9); a spend in the mempool (0) counts even less.

cases.name: coins confirmed at anchor-144 pass
cases.why: confirmed_at <= anchor - dir_floor_confs.

cases.name: coins confirmed at anchor-143 fail
cases.why: Too young at the anchor: fails for good, and the next claim holds.

cases.name: no coin answer before the holder
cases.why: §8.2.5 (4): passing over an unread claim would hand the handle to a later one.

cases.name: no binding answer before the holder
cases.why: The same for a binding read.

cases.name: same-block tie goes to the lower claim_id
a tombstone signed by a bound key ends the claim
cases.why: §8.2.4: the next claim holds.

cases.name: the same claim in a listing after its tombstone stays ended
cases.why: §8.2.4: an ended claim_id never counts again.

cases.name: a forged tombstone under an unbound key ends nothing
cases.why: M6: claim_ids are public; only a bound key can end one.

cases.name: a forged newer listing for the holder's address under an unbound key
cases.why: M5: a record signed by an unbound key is nobody's, including as the address's state.

cases.name: an earlier-anchored listing for the holder's address under an unbound key is passed over
cases.why: M5: the address's binding read is made for the earlier record, kept, and the holder's own claim holds.

cases.name: the audit finds a withheld earlier claim
cases.why: §8.2.6: a fully valid claim found only on public relays, anchored before the directory answer, holds.

cases.name: an audit it cannot finish leaves the directory answer
cases.why: §8.2.6: public records never turn a directory answer into E_DIR_UNRESOLVED.

cases.name: a directory walk that stops unresolved lets no later audit claim hold
cases.why: §8.2.6: M1 still holds when the audit has a valid later claim.

cases.name: the legacy entry
cases.why: §8.2.8: the reader treats exactly this v1 listing as carrying the shipped claim (vc22 legacy_claim_id).

cases.name: no header answer for an anchor before the holder
cases.why: §8.2.5 (4): the header for the claim's lowest attestation could not be read, so the claim can be neither placed nor passed over.

cases.name: no header answer for an audit claim leaves the directory answer
cases.why: §8.2.6: the audit claim cannot be finished, so the audit ends and the directory answer stands.

cases.name: 65 failing claims before the holder reach the bound
cases.why: §8.2.5 (5): 64 coin reads, then E_DIR_UNRESOLVED, never contested.

cases.name: the same 65 anchored after the holder are never read
cases.why: Claims after the holder are never read.

cases.name: 65 claims under unbound keys before the holder cost binding reads only
cases.why: §8.2.5 (5): binding reads and coin reads are bounded apart; 66 binding reads, 1 coin read.

cases.name: 257 distinct addresses before a holder reach the binding bound
cases.why: §8.2.5 (5): the 257th address read is past 256: E_DIR_UNRESOLVED.

cases.name: audit reads never spend the directory bounds
cases.why: §8.2.5 (5): 16 audit coin reads count against the audit alone, so the 51 directory coin reads stay under 64 and the holder holds.

cases.name: the 16th audit coin read is still made
cases.why: §8.2.6: 16 coin reads for audit claims; the 16th finds a fully valid earlier claim, which holds.

cases.name: the 17th audit coin read ends the audit
cases.why: §8.2.6: the audit claim that would need a 17th coin read ends the audit, and the directory answer stands.

cases.name: the 64th audit binding read is still made
cases.why: §8.2.6: 64 addresses read for audit claims; the 64th is a fully valid earlier claim, which holds.

cases.name: the 65th audit binding read ends the audit
cases.why: §8.2.6: the audit claim that would need a 65th address read ends the audit, and the directory answer stands.

cases.name: a bech32 address in capitals is dropped before any read
cases.why: §8.2.5 (1): an address is written in its canonical form, a bech32 address in lowercase; the capitalized record is never read.

cases.name: a newer unanchored listing from another of the address's keys does not end its anchored claim
cases.why: §8.2.5 (3): the state is read only from records step 1 kept; the unanchored listing is dropped there, so the anchored claim is still its address's state and holds.

cases.name: audit binding reads never spend the directory binding bound
cases.why: §8.2.5 (5): 64 audit binding reads count against the audit alone, so the 201 directory binding reads stay under 256 and the holder holds; shared counters would make 265.

cases.name: the only claim, ended by its own tombstone, is revoked
cases.why: §8.2.5 (6): the walk ends without a holder, and a tombstone signed by a bound key is the state of an address it read: E_DIR_REVOKED.

cases.name: a freshest tombstone ending another claim leaves the address's older listing no weight
cases.why: §8.2.5 (3): the address's state is its freshest record, here a tombstone, so its listing is not the state and its claim is never read; the next claim holds.

notes: An anchor is a height, or {unread: h} when the header for its lowest attestation could not be read. coin.confirmed_at is the height the claim's outpoint confirmed at; spend.confirmations is the spending transaction's depth (0 = mempool); a spend ends a claim at dir_repoint_blocks + 6 confirmations (§8.2.2 (3)). Keys and the addresses in the padding cases are labels. Re-points are in vc25.
